before:
If your stomach tightens while your little one waits for an answer, slower exhales like before may help you stay with them. Feeling calmer doesn't mean their complaint is wrong, though, and it won't make them trust you on its own.

(That was the end of the previous section. This paragraph is the first one under the new heading:)

after: "I know you're in there. I love you. You don't have to love me back or trust me yet. I can't promise that nothing painful will happen. Or that I'll always know what to do, or never react badly. But I can promise to tell you the truth and listen when you're angry. I'll make our life together safer where I can, and take the next step I can see to protect you. When I fail, I'll come back to make it right. You don't have to believe these words. Watch what I do."

Otherwise, you can make it with or without a visualization of the two of you playing on a swing:
